title: Salisbury Steak with Onion Gravy
subtitle: tender seasoned beef patties simmered in a rich caramelized-onion gravy, over buttery mashed potatoes
imageAlt: Oval beef patties smothered in brown onion gravy beside mashed potatoes on a white plate on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Get the potatoes boiling first; the patties and gravy take about the same time.
Mix the patties gently with your hands: overworked beef turns tough.

items.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
items.note: peeled and cut in 5 cm chunks

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water by 2 cm, add the salt and bring to a boil. Simmer 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides through.

steps.title: Mix the patties
steps.text: Gently mix the beef, panko, egg, milk, ketchup, Worcestershire, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper. Shape into 4 ovals about 2 cm thick.

steps.title: Brown the patties
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high and brown the patties 3–4 minutes a side. They finish cooking in the gravy. Move to a plate.

steps.title: Onions
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, add the butter and onion and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.

steps.title: Gravy
steps.text: Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute. Whisk in the broth a little at a time, then the Worcestershire and dried thyme, and bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Simmer the patties
steps.text: Return the patties and their juices, cover and simmer 10–12 minutes, turning once, until they reach 71°C (160°F) and the gravy has thickened.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Drain the potatoes, return them to the pot for 1 minute to dry, and mash with the warm milk, butter and salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the patties on the mash with plenty of onion gravy.

fixIt.fix: Brown them without moving for the first 3 minutes so a crust forms before flipping.
Whisk hard, or strain it before returning the patties. Add the broth gradually next time.
Whisk in a splash of broth or water.
Mix just until combined and keep the simmer gentle.

saleTip: Buy the ~1 kg family pack of lean ground beef on sale and use the extra for tacos or sloppy joes later in the week.
swap: Ground turkey: same method, simmered to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Reheat patties in their gravy; they also make a great sandwich on a toasted bun.
doneness: 71°C (160°F) in the centre of the thickest patty (Health Canada, ground beef). Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested Salisbury steak methods (Canadian Living, Betty Crocker): seasoned beef patties browned, then simmered in a flour-thickened beef-broth onion gravy.
prepAhead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead; keep covered in the fridge.
Freeze cooked patties in their gravy up to 3 months.
reheat: Covered in a pan over medium-low with a splash of broth or water, 8–10 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Simple patties with salt, pepper and garlic powder, and a plain onion gravy.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the ketchup, Worcestershire and onion powder.
stepNotes.4: Basic: broth only, no Worcestershire or dried thyme.

fancy.note: A splash of cream in the gravy and brown-butter mash.

stepNotes.5: Fancy: stir the cream into the gravy for the last 2 minutes.
stepNotes.6: Fancy: brown the mash butter in a small pan 2–3 minutes until nutty before adding.

plating: Mash in a swoosh, patty leaning on it.
Onions piled on top, gravy spooned around.
Buttered peas or green beans on the side.

why.0-1: Breadcrumbs soaked with milk and egg keep the patties tender and juicy.
why.1-1: Slowly browned onions make the gravy deep, rich and sweet.

funFact: Salisbury steak is named after Dr. James Salisbury, an American physician who promoted minced beef as health food in the 1880s.

keeps.note: freeze patties in their gravy; make fresh mash
